title: Celtic vs. Motherwell referee John Beaton kept under police surveillance, Scottish FA says
content:
The referee for Celtic’s win over Motherwell was under police surveillance on Thursday night after someone leaked his personal details online, the Scottish Football Association said on Friday.

John Beaton awarded Celtic a controversial 99th-minute winning penalty on Wednesday, which ensured the Scottish title race will go down to the final day of the season. The decision was labelled as “disgusting” by league-leading Hearts’ manager Derek McInnes, while Motherwell manager Jens Berthel Askou called it a “shame for the game”.

The SFA called the subsequent reaction an “inevitable consequence of the heightening criticism, intolerance and scapegoating” of match officials and condemned the compromising of their safety “a scourge on our national game”.

“This is the consequence of a hysterical media narrative, fuelled by irresponsible knee-jerk post-match media interviews, commentary and official social media posts,” the SFA statement said on Friday. “The cumulative effect impacts on our ability to provide enough referees to service our game at all levels. When it compromises the safety and wellbeing of our most senior match officials, enough is enough.”

During Wednesday’s game, Celtic’s Auston Trusty had gone down in stoppage time after it appeared he had been caught by Motherwell’s Sam Nicholson’s elbow. Referee Beaton was subsequently sent to the monitor to check for a handball, for which he gave a penalty. The spot-kick was converted, putting Martin O’Neill’s side just one point behind leaders Hearts, whom they will host on Saturday.

“Referees are not infallible,” the SFA statement continued. “Mistakes will be made on the field, and subjective calls made in front of the Video Assistant Referee monitor, just as managers will pick the wrong team, goalkeepers concede soft goals and strikers miss from five yards out. Yet the reaction to these inevitabilities could not be more contrasting.

“What happened yesterday is not an isolated incident. There are many examples of match officials being placed in harmful situations but with individuals fearful of speaking out lest it exacerbates the situation or causes further alarm to friends, family and colleagues.

“We will not allow this to become the norm. We will not allow a situation where match officials require special provision to protect their children at school to be considered an occupational hazard. We will not allow a situation where staying at home with the front door locked and avoiding the hazards of public interaction becomes a coping strategy.”

The Scottish football governing body additionally said it would seek to strengthen its rules and urged “tolerance and perspective”.

Hearts are first in the Scottish Premiership heading into the final day, with Rangers one point behind them and Celtic three points down. Rangers will face Falkirk on Saturday while Celtic host the league leaders on the same day.
